policy.confirmed: Participants, date and the stated start time were read back from an official league/tour governing-body endpoint or page during this cycle. Claimed venue/time that the source does not state is blanked, not kept.
policy.partial: Part of the claim (e.g. the tournament and one round) was confirmed; the rest was not and is blanked/flagged.
policy.unverified: Nothing in the row could be confirmed on an official source in this cycle. Time and venue are blanked, the pick is retained only as our own model output at LOW confidence and the prediction text is withdrawn.
policy.confidenceRule: HIGH requires both sides' current form to be read from an official feed and quoted here. MEDIUM requires a verified fixture plus at least one verified form fact. Everything else is LOW.

NHL05.text: Buffalo Sabres to win at home against Philadelphia on 21 October. Buffalo are 4-3-2 and average 3.00 goals per game, while Philadelphia are 2-6-3 and manage only 1.55 goals per game, the lowest rate in the NHL according to the official game-center feed, with a 12.9% power play that ranks 27th. Philadelphia have won their last two against Colorado and Ottawa, but that followed a 2-5-3 stretch. Buffalo's own special teams are poor, at 9.1% on the power play and 64.5% on the penalty kill, yet the five-on-five scoring gap and home ice make the Sabres moneyline at our 1.90 the selection.

NHL07.text: Florida Panthers to win in Ottawa on 21 October. The Panthers are 5-2-2 and on a three-game run of wins over Seattle, Vancouver in overtime and Columbus, scoring 3.33 goals per game, tenth in the league, while conceding 2.78. Ottawa's 6-3-0 start is built on defence rather than offence: they score 2.44 goals per game, 25th in the NHL, and their power play converts just 12.8%, 29th. Florida also hold the better special-teams numbers, with a 20.9% power play against Ottawa's 12.8%, so the Panthers moneyline at our 1.86 is the pick.

NHL08.text: Boston Bruins to win against Nashville at TD Garden on 22 October. Boston are 7-2-1 and have scored 3.60 goals per game, seventh in the NHL, while conceding only 2.20, fourth, with a 52.7% faceoff rate that ranks sixth; their last ten include wins over Los Angeles, Anaheim, San Jose, Philadelphia and Utah. Nashville are 3-2-3 and score 2.88 goals per game, 22nd in the league, although their power play is dangerous at 29.6%. Boston's five-on-five control and home ice make the Bruins moneyline at our 1.72 the pick.

MLB01.pick: Milwaukee Brewers to win Game 1 (moneyline, our 1.78)
MLB01.text: Milwaukee Brewers to win World Series Game 1 against Tampa Bay at American Family Field on 23 October. MLB's official schedule places the opener at 8:00 p.m. ET with the Rays as the visiting side, and the same feed puts Games 1 and 2 in Milwaukee. Tampa Bay finished the regular season 98-64 and were 43-38 on the road, so they are a genuine opponent rather than a soft draw. We price Milwaukee at 1.78 and the total at 8.0, but this stays a medium-confidence selection because Milwaukee's full-season record could not be re-read from the official standings feed during this cycle.

NHL09.text: New York Rangers +1.5 on the puck line in Toronto on 22 October is the value play. The Rangers concede only 2.18 goals per game, third in the NHL, kill penalties at 94.1%, second, and win 53.9% of faceoffs, third, so even a quiet offensive night keeps this inside one goal on the road. Toronto score 3.45 a game, eighth, with the league's best penalty kill at 97.4%, but they also concede 3.09, sixteenth, which is too leaky to trust by a two-goal margin at our 1.48.
